description: Label and name text repaired in map source files. Each entry restores characters that were damaged to U+FFFD (a wrong-encoding decode where a fada was) or stored decomposed (a combining accent after its letter). packages/maps-pipeline/src/tiles/repair-label-text.mjs applies it to the local source FlatGeobufs before the tiles are rebuilt (keyed readings only at the confidence levels listed under apply); scripts/check/rules/map-label-data.mjs --sources accepts a damaged source value only while a repair here covers it.

methods.osm-townland: the same townland in OpenStreetMap (name:ga, from Logainm)
methods.osm-cork-object: the same place in OpenStreetMap, Co. Cork (name:ga, from Logainm)
methods.osi-townland: the same townland name in the OSi townland file (Townlands_AllIreland, Cork)
methods.irish-word-pattern: each damaged word matches one word in the clean Irish townland names (OSi, Logainm via OpenStreetMap)
methods.manual: read by hand: one fada vowel restored in a common word

confidence.medium: one plausible reading; worth a Logainm check
confidence.open: not settled: the Irish name is left empty until checked

apply.note: Which keyed readings repair-label-text.mjs writes into the sources. The owner accepted the high-confidence readings in bulk on 12 Nov 2026, and eight more places (16 records, IN1 and IN2) on 13 Nov 2026; the open ones stay in the sources as they are (still damaged) until the owner settles each. To accept one, raise its confidence to high and say who decided in its note. A record with no confidence is certain and always applies.

translink-bus-stops-2024.note: The apostrophes were right single quotation marks (U+2019); the trailing damage on three Old Mill stops is dropped. Taobh an tStrúthain (Brookside), LocationID 16085, AtcoCode 700000016002 (Co. Donegal, 55.13900 N, 7.45050 W): Translink's own spelling, read from its Bus Stop List on OpenDataNI (dataset translink-bus-stop-list), whose January 2018 CSV and earlier CSV (Windows-1252) store byte 0xFA, ú, where the 2024 GeoJSON export (export10042024.geojson, this layer's source) has U+FFFD. Translink's current list (bus-stop-export-20260923.xlsx, fetched 12 Nov 2026) no longer includes the stop. Translink writes tStrúthain; the standard Irish for Brookside is Taobh an tSrutháin, but a stop keeps the operator's own name.

nfc.note: Every string attribute is normalised to NFC. These sources carried "Dún Braoin" as u + U+0301.
